HTTP Observatory

Grade every site a FortiWeb server policy or FortiADC virtual server publishes with the MDN HTTP Observatory tests and scoring, see whether the FortiWeb, the application or the certificate caused each finding, and apply the FortiWeb fix with a preview of the grade it gives.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsmonitoring.view protection.apply operations.apply
📍 WhereTroubleshooting → HTTP Observatory (Global, FortiWeb and FortiADC ADOMs) (URL /observatory/)

What is it?#

The HTTP Observatory grades the sites your appliances publish the way the MDN HTTP Observatory (developer.mozilla.org/observatory) grades a public site: twelve tests, a score that starts at 100, and a letter from A+ to F. Unlike a public scanner it knows the configuration of the FortiWeb in front of the site, so for every result it says who produced it — the FortiWeb, the application or the certificate — and offers the FortiWeb change that fixes it.

What does it do?#

  • Lists the published sites of the appliance you pick: one row per FortiWeb server policy or FortiADC virtual server, with its VIP, the HTTP and HTTPS ports it serves and a site name (the Host and SNI of the requests).
  • Lets you choose which of them to work on: Select sites is a searchable checkbox list (policy, site name, Protected Hostnames, VIP), and only the ticked sites appear in the table. Searching never unticks; the selection is remembered per appliance in your browser.
  • Grades one site (Grade) or every ticked one (Grade selected), with the tests and scoring of the MDN HTTP Observatory, algorithm version 6.
  • Explains each test: the result, its score modifier, who produced it and what to do.
  • Fixes on the FortiWeb: header rows, HSTS, the HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect and cookie flags, with a preview of every write, of the server policies it reaches and of the grade it would give. The site is graded again afterwards.
  • Reverts a fix: every applied set of fixes is kept with what each write changed, and Revert undoes it — never overwriting what someone changed since.
  • Deploys a Content Security Policy in two steps: Report-Only first (it blocks nothing), then enforced.
  • Uses the HSTS preload list as mozilla.org does, so a preloaded site gets its +5.
  • Exports the sites of an appliance as CSV and a result as a PDF report.
  • Keeps a history of grades per site, and grades every night with the scheduled action HTTP Observatory — grade published sites (armed by default).
  • From the Transaction Tracer, a line under the legs shows the security-header grade of leg A's response and links here.

Requirements#

  • A FortiWeb or FortiADC appliance SATOM can read.
  • The SATOM server must reach the VIP of the policy on its HTTP/HTTPS ports.
  • For fixes: a FortiWeb whose server policy has a Web Protection Profile (for the header and cookie fixes) and, for the redirect, both an HTTP and an HTTPS service.

Permissions#

Action Needs
Open the page, list sites, Grade, History Any read permission (the coarse view key, for example monitoring.view)
Export CSV, PDF report Any read permission
Preview changes, Apply and Revert The coarse config_write key, for example protection.apply
HSTS preload list Refresh now and Import file operations.apply

Users without config_write see the findings and the fixes as text marked (needs config write); the Fix on the FortiWeb card is not drawn. Grading needs no free-target permission: SATOM dials only the VIP of a policy on an appliance visible to you, never an address you type.

How to use#

Grade the sites of an appliance#

  1. Open Troubleshooting → HTTP Observatory and pick the appliance.
  2. Open Select sites, search, and tick the sites to grade. Select all matches ticks what the search shows; the ✕ on a row removes a site.
  3. Check the Site name of each row. It defaults to the first plain name of the policy's Protected Hostnames, otherwise the VIP. Type the name your users browse to — it is sent as Host and SNI, so a name-based site answers as it does for them.
  4. Click Grade on a row, or Grade selected.
  5. The Result card shows the grade, the score, how many tests passed, the previous grade, the redirect routes, the certificate check and, when the certificate is not trusted, the grade the site would get with a trusted one.

Read a result#

Each test row shows the test, its modifier (+5, -20…), the result and a Who badge:

Badge Meaning
FortiWeb The appliance sets it: an HTTP Header Security row, HSTS or the redirect on the server policy, or its own cookiesession1 cookie. A header the profile adds replaces the application's.
Application The backend sent it; the FortiWeb passes it through.
Certificate The points are lost to an untrusted certificate (HSTS and the redirect test fail whatever the headers say).
Not sent Nobody sends it.

Trace this request opens the Transaction Tracer on the site.

Fix findings on the FortiWeb#

  1. In the result, tick the fixes you want and adjust their options (header value, Content Security Policy text, HSTS max-age, cookie flags).
  2. Click Preview changes. You get the writes in order, the server policies they affect and Grade now … → after these fixes ….
  3. If other server policies share the profile, they are named and the confirmation tick appears: tick it to apply to all of them.
  4. Click Apply. Each write is re-read from the device (verified), and the site is graded again.

Deploy a Content Security Policy without breaking the site#

  1. On a site without a CSP, the Content Security Policy row offers Step 1 — send it as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only. Tick it, edit the policy to list the sources your site uses, Preview changes and Apply. The preview shows the grade does not change: the Observatory scores Report-Only like no CSP.
  2. Browse the site and watch the developer console (or the report-uri the policy names) for what the policy would block. Adjust the policy until nothing legitimate is reported.
  3. Grade again. The finding now names the Report-Only row, and Step 2 — enforce it starts from that exact policy. Apply it.

Revert a fix#

  1. Right after Apply, click Revert these changes — or later, open History: Fixes applied to this site lists every applied set with its writes, and Revert on the one to undo.
  2. The Revert a fix card reads the appliance again and lists, newest write first, what it would do: will undo, left as is (with the reason) or nothing to do.
  3. If other server policies share the profile, tick the confirmation.
  4. Click Revert. The site is graded again.

Export#

  • Export CSV (next to Reload): every published site of the appliance, its site name, ports, latest grade and score, and one column per test with its result code.
  • PDF report (on a result): that result as a document, with who produced each finding and the fixes.

See the history#

Click History in the result: every grade of the site, with who or what started it (manual, scheduled, fix). Open shows that grade with its findings recomputed against the current configuration.

Grade on a schedule#

A node arms HTTP Observatory — grade published sites by itself (daily 05:30, every FortiWeb and FortiADC) and HTTP Observatory — refresh the HSTS preload list (Monday 05:00). On a node installed before these existed, run sudo satom execute seed actions --yes; satom diagnose install reports them missing until then. Edit or retarget them in Scheduled actions. The grading summary starts with Grade dropped: … when a site scored lower than in the previous run.

Keep the HSTS preload list current#

The page footer shows the list: how many names it holds and when it was fetched (older than three weeks is flagged). Refresh now downloads it; on a node without internet access, Import file takes a copy of Chromium's net/http/transport_security_state_static.json. A failed download keeps the stored list.

Configuration#

Fix What SATOM writes Notes
Set X-Frame-Options / X-Content-Type-Options / Referrer-Policy / Content-Security-Policy A row in the HTTP Header Security profile of the policy's Web Protection Profile A profile satom-hdr-<policy> is created and attached when there is none; an existing row for that header gets the new value instead of a twin.
Set Cross-Origin-Resource / Opener / Embedder-Policy The same Only on builds whose profile rows accept them (FortiWeb 8.0.6 yes, 7.6.8 no).
CSP step 1 — Report-Only A content-security-policy-report-only row in the same profile Blocks nothing; the grade does not change until step 2. FortiWeb 7.6.8 and 8.0.6 accept it.
Enable HSTS hsts-header, hsts-max-age (31536000 by default), hsts-include-subdomains, hsts-preload on the server policy Needs an HTTPS service.
Redirect HTTP to HTTPS http-to-https on the server policy Needs an HTTP and an HTTPS service; the FortiWeb answers 301 to the HTTPS port.
Harden FortiWeb's own cookie internal-cookie-secure, -httponly, -samesite on the server policy Secure is added on HTTPS responses only.
Cookie flags for the application's cookies secure-cookie, http-only, samesite on the Cookie Security policy A policy satom-ck-<policy> with security-mode no (no signing or encryption) is created and attached when there is none.

The Content Security Policy fix starts from default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'; form-action 'self'. Edit it to list the sources your site really uses before applying.

Example#

🧪Example — A bare site behind a FortiWeb

shop on fweb-01 grades F (0): no CSP, no HSTS, no X-Frame-Options, a session cookie without Secure or HttpOnly, no redirect to HTTPS, and a self-signed certificate. Ticking every offered fix previews 14 writes and Grade now F 0 → after these fixes C 55. After Apply the site grades C 55; the remaining 40 points are the certificate (the summary says the site would score A+ 145 with a trusted one) and 5 are an external script without SRI, which only the application can fix.

Result#

  • Every grade is stored (60 per site); results keep headers, statuses, redirect routes and cookie flags — never cookie values or page bodies.
  • Every applied set of fixes is stored with its writes and their previous values, so it can be reverted.
  • Audit entries: observatory.scan per grade, observatory.fix per applied set of fixes (with the writes), observatory.fix.refused when a fix was refused, observatory.fix.revert per revert, observatory.export per CSV or PDF, observatory.hsts_preload.refresh / .import.
  • Applied writes also appear in the appliance's change history, like edits made in the object editor.

Troubleshooting#

"not graded" with "the site did not answer"#

Possible causes - The SATOM server cannot reach the VIP on that port (routing, firewall). - The policy is enabled but its back end does not answer.

Solution 1. Open the site in the Transaction Tracer with Trace this request. 2. Fix the reachability, then Grade again.

Verification — the row shows a grade.

"HTTP 500 is not graded (only 2xx, 3xx, 401 and 403 are)"#

Possible causes - The site answered with an error status; the Observatory does not grade error pages.

Solution — fix the application or try another site name, then grade again.

The redirect route ends with "not followed: outside this policy"#

Possible causes - The site redirects to another host or port. SATOM never dials a destination the policy does not publish.

Solution — grade the destination site from its own policy. The redirect test still scores the route it saw.

A fix shows "cannot add this header from HTTP Header Security"#

Possible causes - The appliance's firmware does not offer that header in profile rows (Cross-Origin-* headers on FortiWeb 7.x).

Solution — set the header in the application, or upgrade the appliance.

"Web Protection Profile … is template-managed"#

Possible causes - An approved template governs the profile.

Solution — change it in Template Library; saving an approved template deploys to all devices.

"… is being edited by …; nothing was sent to the device."#

Possible causes - Another user holds the edit lease on an object of the plan.

Solution — wait, or take over the lock (see Locks).

Revert shows "left as is: changed since the fix"#

Possible causes - Someone changed that field (or edited the row) after the fix. SATOM never overwrites a change it did not make.

Solution — the other steps are reverted; change that field by hand if it should go back too. A partly reverted fix can be reverted again later.

Verification — the fix shows reverted in History once nothing is left to undo.

"HSTS preload list: not on this node"#

Possible causes - The node has never downloaded it, or has no internet access.

Solution — Refresh now, or Import file with a copy of Chromium's transport_security_state_static.json. Until then a preloaded site scores 5 below mozilla.org.

HSTS still fails after enabling it#

Possible causes - The certificate is not trusted (Certificate badge). Browsers ignore HSTS over an untrusted session; the test shows the header arrived but cannot pass.

Solution — replace the certificate in Certificate Manager.

Advanced#

Advanced Differences from mozilla.org
  • The HSTS preload list is the node's copy (refreshed weekly); a node without one grades every site as not preloaded.
  • A non-numeric HSTS max-age is scored invalid (mozilla.org passes it).
  • The SRI test's "same site" uses a short built-in list of multi-label public suffixes instead of the full Public Suffix List.
  • Redirects are followed only while they stay on the scanned policy.
Advanced What is fetched

https://<site>/ and http://<site>/ with their redirects (up to 10), /robots.txt, and an OPTIONS preflight with Origin: https://observatory.satom.invalid for the CORS test. The certificate is checked against the SATOM server's trust store; the request is made either way.

Advanced How a revert writes

Newest write first. Within one object, the values come back before the switch that governs them is turned off, and each switch is turned off in a write of its own: FortiWeb answers 200 and silently keeps the old value of a dependent field sent in the same request that disables its switch (hsts-max-age and hsts-include-subdomains with hsts-header disable, measured on 8.0.6). Every write is re-read from the device, so a dropped field shows as mismatch.

Advanced Which header values a build accepts

SATOM reads the choices of the profile-row fields per firmware build from the API library (the CLI tree of that build). A build that was never measured offers only X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Content-Security-Policy and Referrer-Policy.
